sentences.text: Hollardosteus marocanus is a Middle Devonian arthrodire placoderm found in Morocco.
Remains of this fish were found in Eifelian-aged strata from the Tafilat-Maider Valley.
The lower jaw plate of Hollardosteus has a well-developed anterior tooth that resembles those of dunkleosteids.
The armor of Hollardosteus features a pattern of large, crowded tubercles, unlike the smooth armor of dunkleosteids.
The species was described by Lehman in 1976.
Hollardosteus belongs to the parent group Arthrodira.
It is classified in the class Placodermi.
Due to its unique features, Hollardosteus is currently classified as Arthrodira incertae sedis pending more complete specimens.
Hollardosteus lived during the Eifelian stage.
